method: Static PE inspection, cleave facts including decoded text, Rizin execution-path analysis, Go objdump, and independent XOR TLV decoding; no sample executed.

samples.identity: Configured x86 Cobalt Strike DNS Beacon reflective DLL
evidence: Export _ReflectiveLoader@4 at VA 0x10008c79 walks PE headers, resolves loader APIs, allocates executable image memory, copies sections, processes imports/relocations and invokes the mapped entry point.
VA 0x10009619 XOR-decodes 4096 settings bytes with 0x69, parses typed length-value records and erases the decoded source table. File offset 0x2f228 contains the encoded table.

Decoded settings include a public key, ns7/ns8/ns9.softline.top endpoints, port 443, 5000 ms sleep, HTTP cover headers impersonating www.amazon.com, and rundll32 spawn paths. These are configuration observations, not evidence of contact during this review.

VA 0x100015c4 repeatedly checks for tasking and sleeps. DNS response bytes are reconstructed by the A/TXT/AAAA transport helpers, passed through 0x100092b8, then dispatched by 0x100014a0 to command handler 0x10001000.

VA 0x1000357b requests TXT records through DnsQuery_A, concatenates record strings into the destination buffer, and frees results using DnsFree. VA 0x1000361b requests AAAA records and copies their 16 data bytes. VA 0x100025f1 reconstructs response data from DNS A-record values using generated cdn labels.
samples.trait_changes: Add notable ANSI DNS-query and DNS-result-release API observations; require a DNS query API in the hostile DNS Beacon template fingerprint. Remove the DNS C2 ATT&CK mapping from ordinary native DNS API observations; the family fingerprint retains its supported C2 mapping.

samples.identity: Go ZIP downloader/launcher carrying the same configured Beacon DLL
evidence: The complete 351213-byte overlay starting at file offset 0x4bc201 is byte-for-byte identical to the first sample. It is an embedded configured implant, rather than an incidental Beacon word match.
main.checkForAdmin at VA 0x58ecd0 tests whether it can open \\.\PHYSICALDRIVE0; this is an access check, not a disk-write operation.

Without administrative access, main.main constructs Start-Process -FilePath followed by its own path and -Verb runAs, then starts powershell.exe. This requests user-approved elevation; no UAC bypass was established.

The elevated path checks/creates a TEMP/GData.txt marker, downloads pieghevole.zip from an S3 endpoint, extracts it under C:/G DATA Security Software/, removes the ZIP and launches AVK.exe. main.GetArchive binds HTTP response body copying to the output file; main.Extract opens ZIP members and writes their extracted content.

The hostname query result is not shown flowing to a send; no hostname exfiltration is claimed. The Go main path was not shown executing the appended DLL, so that relationship is recorded only as containment.
samples.trait_changes: The embedded DLL receives the same DNS coverage and strengthened family fingerprint; no filename exception or dependent-only suppression.

samples.identity: Modified StormAttack persistence/injection loader with erased resource directory
evidence: The entry point calls 0x401cb0. Its selected mode is 3, which calls 0x401900 for Active Setup persistence and then 0x401390 for shell self-deletion.

VA 0x401900 constructs a GUID executable path, creates an HKLM Active Setup Installed Components key and writes the copied executable path as StubPath. It reads its own image with CRT I/O, patches bytes, writes the new image and launches it.
VA 0x401390 derives the current module's short path, builds a COMSPEC /c del command with output redirection, and launches the cleanup process.

Other retained branches attempt resource DLL extraction through 0x402460, replace LanmanServer Parameters/ServiceDLL through 0x401260 and inject the DLL path using VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory and CreateRemoteThread at 0x401150. The thread entry is the resolved LoadLibraryA export.

The 40032 bytes of declared resource data are all zero, so resource extraction cannot yield the intended DLL. Installation/injection success and DDoS operation are not established for these bytes. The existing hostile descriptions explicitly describe retained code/API profiles.
Appended nonstandard sections contain unrelated application/library text. Ransomware, browser theft and network contact are not inferred from those fragments or the collector-assigned filename.
samples.trait_changes: no change; existing four hostile traits and one suspicious injection trait accurately describe the retained malicious code, without claiming successful deployment.

controls: check.py verifies ANSI and Unicode query variants, import-versus-plain-text distinction, result cleanup without a query, query without cleanup, and absent required template/diagnostic evidence.
scope_audit: No exact external consumers of dnsapi-lookup were found. The existing communications/dns/lookup directory consumer in metadata/file/profile/operation-cooccurrence/runner-network-observations.yaml remains a neutral co-occurrence observation. Cleanup and name-comparison atoms remain visible independently but no longer satisfy a query claim.
external_report: The supplied tria.ge report could not be retrieved. Verdicts above are based on sample bytes and recovered execution paths.
